title: Retention controls + baseline compliance reporting pack (Hosted/Dedicated/Private)
creator: Naomi Feldman
description:
Context
Regulated customers evaluating Dedicated and Private deployments are increasingly blocked on two repeatable items during security/procurement: (1) clear, enforceable retention controls across key data classes and (2) a standardized, customer-ready compliance evidence package that can be generated on-demand.

This initiative productizes retention configuration (policy schema, UX, enforcement + verification) and delivers a baseline “Compliance Reporting Pack” that reduces sales/CS overhead and shortens security review cycles.

Scope (v1)
1) Retention controls
- Customer-configurable retention controls with safe defaults by tier (Hosted / Dedicated / Private).
- Supported data classes in v1:
  - Request/response logs (where stored)
  - Audit logs
  - Traces + metrics (retention config + verification, where applicable)
  - Artifacts tied to compliance workflows (e.g., retention config export, report pack artifacts)
- Behavior clarity:
  - TTL semantics (time basis, evaluation location, and enforcement cadence)
  - Purge semantics (idempotent deletes, retries, backfill, verification)
  - Legal hold / incident holds + documented exceptions
  - Change history + audit trail for policy updates

2) Baseline compliance reporting pack (MVP)
Customer-facing, time-windowed package that includes:
- Audit-log coverage summary + export for a given time window
- Retention configuration export (current + change history window)
- Data residency / region summary (deployment + audit export region constraints)
- Access control / RBAC summary (roles, admin actions, relevant permission model)
- Evidence collection checklist aligned to SOC 2 / ISO-style control expectations

Non-goals (v1)
- Full custom report builder or deep “bring your own GRC” integrations beyond standard exports.
- Arbitrary per-field redaction policies (handled separately under logging standards).

Primary personas / users
- Customer Security Admin: wants configurable retention and exportable evidence.
- Auditor / GRC: wants standardized evidence and repeatable generation procedure.
- SRE / On-call: wants retention changes to not compromise debugging; needs break-glass + clear exception workflow.
- Sales Engineering / CS: wants consistent, approved language and artifacts to unblock security reviews.

Milestones + target timeline
Phase 0 — Requirements + inventory (target: 2025-01-21 → 2025-02-04)
- Complete data inventory for in-scope stores (request logs, audit logs, telemetry stores) and confirm ownership.
- Align terminology and definitions (audit logs vs request logs; what constitutes “stored prompts/completions”).
- Draft retention policy schema and validation rules by tier.
Exit criteria:
- Sign-off from Security (Marcus Lin) + GRC (Olga Petrov) on definitions and v1 scope.

Phase 1 — Retention policy service + enforcement for core stores (target: 2025-02-05 → 2025-03-07)
- Control plane: CRUD policy API, validation, change history, policy evaluation + caching.
- Data plane: TTL enforcement for request logs + audit logs, purge job framework, backfills, and verification metrics.
- Initial console surface: view effective retention + last change; gated editing per RBAC.
Exit criteria:
- Idempotent purge jobs in place with SRE-approved safety limits.
- Verification dashboards show TTL lag and purge success for design partner tenants.
- Documentation draft ready for Security review.

Phase 2 — Compliance reporting pack MVP (target: 2025-03-03 → 2025-03-21)
- Report generator MVP: time-windowed audit log export + attach retention config export.
- Standard templates aligned to evidence needs (customer and internal audit).
- Console download flow (or support-assisted flow) and docs/FAQ for how to request.
Exit criteria:
- “Baseline compliance pack” generated end-to-end for at least 2 pilot customers with repeatable steps.
- Output versioned; backwards compatibility expectations documented.

Phase 3 — Staged rollout + GA criteria (target: 2025-03-17 → 2025-03-28)
- Staged rollout: internal → design partners → broader enterprise.
- Finalize runbooks, alert thresholds, support playbooks.
- GA sign-off checklist completed.
Exit criteria:
- GA readiness sign-off from Security, SRE, and Product.
- Customer-facing enablement ready (SE brief + internal FAQ).

Success criteria (what “done” means)
Product outcomes
- Retention controls available (with tiered defaults) across Hosted/Dedicated/Private where supported, with a single source-of-truth policy and customer-visible effective retention.
- Compliance Reporting Pack MVP can be generated on-demand for a specified time window with standardized contents.
- Legal hold / incident hold workflow documented, auditable, and enforced in the retention evaluation path.

Operational outcomes
- Purge jobs are idempotent, observable, and safe to rerun; backlog and failures are alerting.
- No measurable performance regression in telemetry pipelines attributable to purge/enforcement.
- Clear break-glass guidance that balances short retention with incident response needs.

GTM outcomes
- Reduce time spent by Sales Engineering / CS on security reviews by standardizing retention answers and providing a customer-ready evidence pack.
- Target: unblock at least 2 enterprise deals where retention/reporting was a procurement blocker.

Rollout plan (by deployment tier)
Hosted
- Default retention: conservative baseline aligned to current operational norms; allow shorter retention (within min TTL) for enterprise tenants.
- Console: retention view/edit gated by org admin + security admin roles.
- Compliance pack: generated via console request or support-assisted workflow depending on tenant tier.

Dedicated
- Same policy surface; defaults set to enterprise-friendly baseline.
- Ensure purge jobs respect tenant isolation and dedicated storage topology.
- Compliance pack: customer can request pack scoped to their dedicated environment and region.

Private (VPC/on-prem)
- Provide secure defaults and infrastructure prerequisites (storage/backing services) for purge jobs.
- Where direct console access is constrained, provide CLI/API exports and documented procedure.
- Compliance pack: generator may run in-customer environment; define what Redwood can attest to vs customer-operated evidence.

Risks / open questions
- Data class boundary: confirm exact meaning of “prompts/completions where stored” and ensure docs don’t imply we persist payloads when logging is disabled.
- Min/max TTL per tier: avoid configurations that make on-call debugging impossible without break-glass; document exceptions and approval matrix.
- Multi-region enforcement: ensure TTL lag metrics and exports reflect data residency constraints (no cross-region export leakage).
- Customer expectations for “immediate deletion”: we must be explicit about enforcement cadence, eventual consistency, and verification signals.

Notes for execution
- Keep customer-facing terminology consistent and review by Legal (Sofia Mendes) before external sharing.
- Treat verification dashboards and runbooks as GA blockers (not “nice to have”).
updates: 2025-02-04 (Naomi): Phase 0 complete. Locked v1 data classes (request logs + audit logs + telemetry retention config/verification). Legal hold semantics to be documented as an exception/override with audit trail; implementation to land behind admin-only permissions.

2025-02-18 (Naomi): Design partner candidates confirmed with GTM: Northbridge Bank (Dedicated), Photon Health (Private). Success criterion updated: must generate baseline pack for at least two pilots before GA.
2025-03-06 (Naomi): Flagging risk from SRE: purge backlogs after maintenance windows. GA blocker added: dashboards + alert thresholds must be in place and on-call runbook validated.
